Peptide Dosing Math

A lyophilized peptide vial is labelled in milligrams of powder. A syringe is marked in units. The answer depends on how much bacteriostatic water you added.

Concentration

concentration (mg/mL) = vial strength (mg) / water added (mL)

A 5 mg vial with 2 mL of bacteriostatic water is 2.5 mg/mL.

Volume for a dose

volume (mL) = dose (mg) / concentration (mg/mL)

A 0.25 mg dose from a 2.5 mg/mL vial is 0.1 mL.

Volume to syringe units

A U-100 insulin syringe is graduated so that 100 units equal 1 mL.

units = volume (mL) x 100

0.1 mL is 10 units. That is the number you read off the barrel.

If the dose lands between marks, change the reconstitution volume so the syringe units are easier to draw.

None of this is medical advice. The arithmetic is arithmetic; the dose itself is a question for whoever is prescribing it.
